newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cen.bank to allow Lombard rate to float.
newsitem.headline: Romania cen.bank to allow Lombard rate to float.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu said the Lombard rate, now at an annual 90 percent, would be allowed to float starting this week aligned to the one-week rate on auctioned refinancing credits.
"The Lombard rate will be set weekly by multiplying the average one-week auctioned rate by 1.6 percent," Isarescu told a news conference.

So far the BNR has periodically changed the Lombard, which it charges for overdraft credits, according to monetary policy goals. It has been flat at 90 pecent since last April when the BNR cut it from from a previous 100.
"If the one-week auctioned credit rate stays at 90 percent at Thursday's refinancing auction, then starting Friday the Lombard rate will be around 144 percent," Isarescu said.
Last week, the one-week auctioned credit rate jumped to 90 percent from a previous 81 percent, following a recent drive to tighten monetary policies as the BNR tries to control a surge in inflation.

Year-on-year inflation was 56.9 percent last year, almost triple the 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund. Monthly inflation was 10.3 percent last December and a further bob is seen after January's fuel price rise.

Isarescu also said that starting this week, the BNR would no longer set on its own the minimum permitted rate for the one-week auctioned refinancing funds, allowing the market to set the starting price for its funds.
The other BNR key rate, the discount rate, remained flat at 50 percent a year.

"Our refinancing facilities will become more flexible," Isarescu said. "Auctioned credits will hold a larger share of overall refinancing and within one year we plan to introduce open market operations."

Auctioned credits held 20 percent of the BNR's daily refinancing loans last month, when structural loans and credits for the farming sector -- for which the BNR charges its discount rate -- took more than half of the total.

Isarescu said the BNR was seeking to change its structural refinancing facilities, given mainly to the farming sector, in a bid to find alternative ways to solve financing for farming. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
